cast.name: Humbert Humbert
cast.role: The narrator — a European émigré literature professor in his late 30s, writing a confession from a prison cell. Suave, erudite, manipulative; weaponizes beautiful prose to disguise predation.
cast.look: Late-30s European man, tall lean build, dark swept-back hair, sharp angular face, wearing a tailored charcoal suit with white shirt and silk tie, professorial air

cast.name: Dolores Haze
cast.role: The real victim — a 12-year-old American girl whom Humbert kidnaps and abuses. Chews gum, reads comics, plays tennis. Her actual voice is the silence Humbert's prose buries.
cast.look: 12-year-old American girl, slight build, brown hair in a ponytail, wearing a plaid cotton dress and white sneakers, freckled face, looks like an ordinary schoolgirl

cast.name: Charlotte Haze
cast.role: Dolores's mother — a lonely, pretentious small-town widow who falls for Humbert. Humbert marries her solely to access Dolores. The comedy Humbert spins around her is the reader's moral anesthetic.
cast.look: Mid-40s American woman, average build, blonde permed hair, wearing a floral print dress with pearl necklace, trying too hard to look sophisticated

cast.name: Clare Quilty
cast.role: The dark mirror — a playwright-pornographer who shadows Humbert across America and eventually lures Dolores away. Simply Humbert without the literary talent to disguise himself.
cast.look: Late-40s American man, heavy build, thinning dark hair, rumpled linen suit, dissolute appearance, cigarette-stained fingers, smirking face

cast.name: Annabel Leigh
cast.role: Humbert's manufactured origin story — a childhood sweetheart on the Riviera who died of typhus. He uses her memory to frame his obsession as romantic fate rather than predation.
cast.look: Young girl around 13, slight build, light brown hair loose to shoulders, wearing a white summer dress, Mediterranean seaside setting

cast.name: Vladimir Nabokov
cast.role: The author — discussed as the architect behind the trap. Built the novel so that the reader experiences how seductive rhetoric manufactures consent for the inexcusable.
cast.look: 50s Russian-American man, stocky build, receding gray hair, round face, wearing a tweed jacket with bow tie, butterfly-collector air
